questions.question: An Exile takes the Oathkeeper title during their Act phase. When can they first win as Usurper, and what happens if someone takes the title away meanwhile?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: At their next Wake they check victory before flipping Oathkeeper to Usurper, so cannot yet win as Usurper; if still Usurper at the following Wake they win. Losing the title prevents the win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.

questions.question: How do adviser limits, facedown restrictions, revealing later, and replacing a true Vision work?

questions.observed_answer: Advisers are capped at 3 including facedown; an incoming card that changes limit is checked against the new lowest limit before play, and over-limit discards must happen before the card is played. An Exile may reveal a true Vision as a minor-action play into the separate Vision slot, replacing/discarding the old Vision; true Visions do not consume adviser slots.

questions.question: How are Campaign attack/defense calculated, and how do skulls, hollow swords, ties and sacrifices work?
questions.expected_answer_from_fixed_key: The attacker may collect attack dice up to the number of warbands in their attacking force (normally those on their board), after accounting for any applicable power that changes that force. Then apply the appropriate dice modifiers. Defense shields multiplied by each double (x2,x4,...), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board if pawn at attacker or targeted site; bandits one per targeted site. Attack skulls kill own force immediately; paired hollow swords count one, lone hollow zero. Attack must strictly exceed defense; may sacrifice force warbands +1 each, exactly enough to win, no excess; if unable/decline defender wins.
questions.observed_answer: Attacker selects up to attack-force warbands in attack dice; defender rolls shields, doubled by each double-symbol (multipliers stack), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board force only if pawn is at attacker/targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only. Each skull kills one attacking-force warband; full swords count, each pair of hollow swords adds one, leftover hollow sword zero. Attacker may sacrifice surviving force for +1 per warband, but exactly enough to win. Attack must strictly exceed defense; tie is defender win.
